title: Entropy
body:
[[Shannon Entropy]]
Can be used to measure expected [[Information]]
[[Cross-Entropy]]

---

Evan's middle line is the definition, and **[[Shannon Entropy]] is the real note**: this one is the
disambiguation, because the word carries three meanings in a CS degree and only one of them is the
formula.

| Sense | What it measures | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Information entropy** | expected [[Information]] in bits, $-\sum P\log P$ | this course, [[Shannon Entropy]] |
| Thermodynamic entropy | the number of microstates a system can be in | physics, not the vault |
| "Entropy" as decay | code rot, disorder as a metaphor | prose, not a quantity |

The first two are genuinely related: both count $\log(\text{number of arrangements})$, and Shannon
took the name on von Neumann's advice partly because the formula matched Boltzmann's. That is a
real connection, not a pun, but the units and the subject matter differ and no argument in this
course crosses between them.

## The one place the word appears without "Shannon"

**Decision trees.** A split is chosen to maximise *information gain*, which is the entropy of the
labels before the split minus the weighted average entropy after it. A split that separates the
classes cleanly leaves low-entropy children and scores well; a split that leaves both children as
mixed as the parent gains nothing. That is [[Shannon Entropy]]'s formula applied to a
[[Classification]] label distribution, and it is the standard use of "entropy" in
[[MACHINE LEARNING]] outside the loss function. The [[Tree]] structure itself is
[[INFORMATION STRUCTURES]]'.

## Related

- [[Shannon Entropy]]: the definition, the coin table, and the maximum-at-uniform fact
- [[Information]]: what is being averaged
- [[Cross-Entropy]] and [[KL Divergence]]: the two-distribution versions
- [[Information Theory]]
- [[Decision Tree]] in [[ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE]] is where this gets **used** rather than
  defined: a tree picks each split to maximise information gain, which is the entropy drop from
  the parent node to the weighted average of its children. A pure node has $H = 0$, so the
  algorithm is walking downhill in entropy on purpose
